chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs Tamattu' during the months of Hajj and then stays in Mecca until Hajj arrives, upon him is a sheep; and whoever performs Tamattu' in other than the months of Hajj and then stays (as a neighbor/resident) until Hajj arrives, there is no blood (sacrifice) upon him. It is an individual Hajj, and the sacrifice (Al-Adha) is upon the people of the cities (Amsar).'
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And whoever entered Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah, up to his saying: 'And whoever arrived at Arafat'.
For the explanation of that has already passed previously, so there is no need to repeat it, because there is sufficiency in that location.

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And whoever arrived at Arafat before the rising of the dawn on the Day of Sacrifice, he has caught it; and if he did not arrive until the dawn rose, he has missed it. And if he arrived at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram before the rising of the sun on the Day of Sacrifice, he has caught the Hajj; so if he did not arrive until the sun rose, he has missed the Hajj.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid Hajj regarding presence at Arafat and the required sacrifices for Tamattu'?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates on the distinction between Tamattu' and Qiran by specifying that the sacrificial animal (dam) is obligatory only for those who remain in Mecca during the Hajj months, whereas those residing outside are exempt, reflecting the Shia view that the sacrifice is tied to the specific state of confinement in the holy city. The text further refines the temporal validity of the Hajj pillars, establishing that presence at Arafat before dawn and at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram before sunrise are critical thresholds for the ritual's acceptance.
